title: Transformations
ks3: Geometry and measures: reflection, rotation, translation, enlargement and symmetry
intro: Flip it, turn it, slide it or make it bigger. Practise reflections, rotations, translations, enlargements and symmetry.
description: Free KS3 Maths transformations questions with answers: reflection, rotation, translation, enlargement and scale factor, line and rotational symmetry. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: Which transformation takes shape A to shape B?
questions.hint: Look at where the right angle is on each shape.
questions.explain: B is the mirror image of A, with the y-axis as the mirror line. A translation would not flip the shape.

questions.q: The point (3, 2) is reflected in the y-axis. Where does it go?
questions.hint: The y-axis is the vertical line. The point flips from right to left.
questions.explain: Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate: (3, 2) → (−3, 2).

questions.q: The point (2, 5) is reflected in the x-axis. Where does it go?
questions.hint: The x-axis is the horizontal line. The point flips from above to below.
questions.explain: Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate: (2, 5) → (2, −5).

questions.q: A shape is reflected in a mirror line. Each point of the image is…
options: the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side
twice as far from the mirror line
on the same side of the mirror line
moved one square to the right
questions.hint: Think of standing in front of a mirror. How far away does your reflection look?
questions.explain: In a reflection, every point moves straight across the mirror line and ends up the same distance away on the other side.

questions.q: The point (4, −1) is reflected in the x-axis. Where does it go?
questions.hint: The x-axis is the horizontal line. Which coordinate changes?
questions.explain: Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate: (4, −1) → (4, 1).

questions.q: The point (5, 3) is reflected in the line x = 2. Where does it go?
questions.hint: x = 2 is a vertical line through 2 on the x-axis. How far is the point from that line?
questions.explain: The point is 5 − 2 = 3 squares to the right of the line, so its image is 3 squares to the left: x = 2 − 3 = −1. The y-coordinate stays 3, so the image is (−1, 3).

questions.q: Which transformation slides a shape without turning or flipping it?
questions.hint: Think of sliding a book across a table.
questions.explain: A translation slides a shape. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.

questions.q: The point (4, 1) is translated 2 squares left and 3 squares up. Where does it go?
questions.hint: Left changes x, up changes y.
questions.explain: Left 2: x = 4 − 2 = 2. Up 3: y = 1 + 3 = 4. So the point goes to (2, 4).

questions.q: After a reflection, a rotation or a translation, the new shape is…
options: exactly the same size and shape (congruent)
questions.hint: None of these three transformations stretches the shape.
questions.explain: Reflections, rotations and translations keep the size and shape the same: the image is congruent to the original. Only enlargement changes the size.

questions.q: Which translation takes shape A to shape B?
questions.hint: Pick one corner of A and count how far it moves across, then how far up, to the same corner of B.
questions.explain: The corner at (1, 1) moves to (4, 2): that is 3 squares right and 1 square up. Every other corner moves the same way.

questions.q: The point (−2, 3) is translated 5 squares right and 4 squares down. Where does it go?
questions.hint: Right adds to x. Down takes away from y.
questions.explain: Right 5: x = −2 + 5 = 3. Down 4: y = 3 − 4 = −1. So the point goes to (3, −1).

questions.q: The point (3, 1) is rotated 180° about the origin (0, 0). Where does it go?
questions.hint: A half turn about the origin sends a point to the opposite side of (0, 0).
questions.explain: A 180° rotation about the origin changes the signs of both coordinates: (3, 1) → (−3, −1).

questions.q: The point (2, 0) is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin. Where does it go?
questions.hint: Start on the positive x-axis and turn a quarter turn anticlockwise.
questions.explain: (2, 0) is on the x-axis, 2 to the right. A quarter turn anticlockwise moves it to the y-axis, 2 up: (0, 2).

questions.q: How many degrees is a quarter turn?
questions.hint: A full turn is 360°.
questions.explain: A quarter of 360° is 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. A half turn is 180°.

questions.q: A shape is rotated 90° clockwise. Which other rotation (about the same centre) gives the same result?
questions.hint: Turning one way and turning the other way add up to a full turn of 360°.
questions.explain: 360° − 90° = 270°, so 90° clockwise ends up in the same place as 270° anticlockwise.

questions.q: The point (1, 3) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin (0, 0). Where does it go?
questions.hint: Try it with tracing paper, or think: a point straight above the origin would end up straight to the right.
questions.explain: A 90° clockwise turn about the origin sends (x, y) to (y, −x), so (1, 3) → (3, −1). (−3, 1) would be 90° anticlockwise, and (−1, −3) would be a half turn.

questions.q: A rectangle 3 cm by 2 cm is enlarged by scale factor 3. What are its new measurements?
questions.hint: Multiply every length by 3.

questions.q: Shape P is 4 cm wide. It is enlarged to make shape Q, which is 10 cm wide. What is the scale factor?
questions.hint: Scale factor = new length ÷ old length.

questions.q: A triangle has an area of 5 cm². It is enlarged by scale factor 2. What is the area of the new triangle?
questions.hint: Both the base and the height double. What happens to base × height?
questions.explain: The base and height both double, so the area is 2 × 2 = 4 times bigger: 5 × 4 = 20 cm². (Not 10!)

questions.q: A photo is 10 cm wide and 15 cm tall. It is enlarged by scale factor 1.5. How tall is the new photo?
questions.hint: Multiply the height by the scale factor.
questions.explain: 15 × 1.5 = 22.5 cm. (The width becomes 10 × 1.5 = 15 cm.)

questions.q: A rectangle 8 cm by 6 cm is enlarged by scale factor {1/2}. What is the area of the new rectangle?
questions.hint: A scale factor of {1/2} makes every length half as long. Find the new lengths first.
questions.explain: The new rectangle is 4 cm by 3 cm, so its area is 4 × 3 = 12 cm². The old area was 48 cm², so the area is a quarter of it, not a half.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.hint: Try folding from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
questions.explain: An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner.

questions.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
questions.hint: How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
questions.explain: A square looks the same after turns of 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°, so it has rotational symmetry of order 4.

questions.q: Which capital letter has rotational symmetry of order 2?
questions.hint: Turn each letter upside down. Which one looks the same?
questions.explain: S looks the same after a half turn, so it has order 2. A, E and T only have line symmetry.

questions.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but no lines of symmetry?
options: A parallelogram (that is not a rectangle or rhombus)
questions.hint: Which one looks the same after a half turn, but can't be folded in half exactly?
questions.explain: A parallelogram looks the same after a half turn (order 2), but folding it never makes the halves match. A rectangle has both kinds; a kite and an isosceles triangle only have a line of symmetry.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (that is not a square) have?
questions.hint: Fold a sheet of paper. Does folding along a diagonal make the halves match?
questions.explain: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry: one across and one down. The diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

questions.q: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a regular hexagon?
questions.hint: How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
questions.explain: A regular hexagon looks the same after every turn of 60°, which happens 6 times in a full turn, so the order is 6.
